issues.title: reader: ZIP as a container format (NST-1..NST-6)
issues.body:
## Goal

A plain zip becomes a document with no blocks of its own and one child per entry, read under the shared budget.

**Requirements:** NST-1, NST-2, NST-3, NST-4, NST-6, SEC-1, SEC-2, SEC-3 — see [docs/prd.md](https://github.com/sanjay3290/docsluice/blob/main/docs/prd.md).

## Context and pointers

- Create `src/readers/zip/index.ts`. Skip directory entries and OS junk (`__MACOSX/`, `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`) — list them with status `skipped`.
- Encrypted entries: status `failed` with code `ENCRYPTED`; set `features.isEncrypted`.
- Child order is central-directory order.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Golden test: a zip holding a CSV, an HTML file, a nested zip, and a PNG.
- [ ] Hostile: nested bombs, quine zip, 10,000 entries, path traversal names — all pass through the runner.
- [ ] `children: "list"` reads no entry data.
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes and CI is green

## Tests required

- [ ] Unit tests
- [ ] Golden tests (corpus files + reviewed expected output)
- [ ] Hostile files added to `hostile/manifest.json`

## Out of scope

- gzip/tar (M3).

## Blocked by

- #4 zip: safe zip reader on fflate with streaming byte counts
- #10 core: reader registry, extract() and nested-file pipeline

issues.title: spike: confirm the PDF engine (ADR 0009)
issues.body:
## Goal

Prove or reject `unpdf` as the PDF engine and record the result in ADR 0009 (status Accepted or Superseded).

**Requirements:** R1, RT-1, RT-2, PDF-10, SEC-10, SEC-11, [ADR 0009](https://github.com/sanjay3290/docsluice/blob/main/docs/adr/0009-pdf-engine.md) — see [docs/prd.md](https://github.com/sanjay3290/docsluice/blob/main/docs/prd.md).

## Context and pointers

- Build a throwaway reader on a branch: load unpdf by dynamic `import()`, get text items with positions per page for 3 corpus PDFs.
- Check in all CI runtimes (Node 20/22/24, Bun, Deno, browser, Workers).
- Check config: `isEvalSupported: false`, no worker, no font/CMap fetching from the network (bundle standard CMaps or skip them with a warning), `disableAutoFetch`, `disableStream`. Prove no network call (stub `fetch`) and no `eval`/`Function` (CSP-like test in the browser job).
- Measure gzipped size of the PDF subpath. Measure time on a 100-page text PDF (PERF-1 target 3 s).
- Compare with `pdfjs-dist` legacy build on the same checks. Use Context7 or the official docs for both.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ADR 0009 updated with a results table (runtime × works, size, time, config used) and a final decision.
- [ ] If accepted: `unpdf` pinned in ADR 0011's table (already listed) and the dependency added in the PDF reader issue, not here.
- [ ] Spike branch is not merged; the PR adds only the ADR change.
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes and CI is green

## Out of scope

- The real reader.

## Blocked by

- #23 ci: cross-runtime matrix — Bun, Deno, browser, Workers (QA-4, RT-1)

## How to work this issue

Follow the loop in [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/sanjay3290/docsluice/blob/main/AGENTS.md): read, check blockers, branch, draft PR, test first, verify, finish. Hard rules and the Definition of Done are in the same file. In Claude Code: `/work-issue <this number>`.

issues.title: pdf: text layer per page, page labels, needsOcr, metadata, outline, links (PDF-1, 4, 6, 10)
issues.body:
## Goal

A text PDF becomes one `section` per page (role `page`, `loc.page`, `loc.pageLabel`) with its text; pages without a text layer are flagged `needsOcr`; metadata, outline and links are read; nothing in the PDF is ever run or fetched.

**Requirements:** PDF-1, PDF-4, PDF-6, PDF-10, SEC-9, SEC-10, SEC-11, [ADR 0009](https://github.com/sanjay3290/docsluice/blob/main/docs/adr/0009-pdf-engine.md) — see [docs/prd.md](https://github.com/sanjay3290/docsluice/blob/main/docs/prd.md).

## Context and pointers

- Create `src/readers/pdf/` with the engine behind `engine.ts` (one module that wraps unpdf so the rest of the reader does not depend on its API).
- Page labels from `/PageLabels` (decimal, roman upper/lower, letters, prefixes, start values).
- needsOcr per page: no text items, or text items that are all whitespace, while the page has image XObjects covering most of the page — set section `needsOcr`, `stats.needsOcr`, add a `NEEDS_OCR` warning with the page numbers. Never return a silent empty result.
- Metadata: Info dictionary + XMP (title, author, dates, language). Outline (bookmarks) → heading blocks placed at their target page. Link annotations → URLs kept in runs (`runs: true`) and `hasExternalLinks`.
- `hasJavaScript` when `/JavaScript`, `/JS`, `/OpenAction` with JS, or `/AA` exist; `/Launch` and `/GoToR`/`/URI` actions are reported, never followed.
- Pages count toward `pdfPages`. Call `budget.tick()` per page and per text item batch.
- In this issue, paragraphs are built naively (items joined by lines in content-stream order). Reading order arrives in pdf2.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Golden tests for corpus PDFs (multi-page, labels, outline, links, scanned page).
- [ ] A scanned PDF gives `needsOcr: true` and a `NEEDS_OCR` warning with page numbers.
- [ ] Hostile: PDF with `/OpenAction` JS, `/Launch`, a remote `/GoToR`, an xref loop, a 100,000-page tree, a deeply nested page tree — all pass with no network call.
- [ ] A 100-page text PDF in under 3 s (record time).
- [ ] The PDF engine loads only when a PDF arrives (bundle test).
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes and CI is green

## Tests required

- [ ] Unit tests
- [ ] Golden tests (corpus files + reviewed expected output)
- [ ] Hostile files added to `hostile/manifest.json`
- [ ] Fuzz target in `packages/docsluice/fuzz/`

## Out of scope

- Reading order (pdf2), encryption (pdf3).

## Blocked by

- #44 spike: confirm the PDF engine (ADR 0009)
- #10 core: reader registry, extract() and nested-file pipeline
- #27 test: LibreOffice corpus pipeline for Office and PDF fixtures (QA-1, R4)

## How to work this issue

issues.title: pdf: reading order — lines, paragraphs, columns (PDF-2)
issues.body:
## Goal

Text items become lines, lines become paragraphs, and two-column pages read column by column, so the output reads like the page.

**Requirements:** PDF-2, DET-1 — see [docs/prd.md](https://github.com/sanjay3290/docsluice/blob/main/docs/prd.md).

## Context and pointers

- Create `src/readers/pdf/layout/`. Input: text items with transform matrix, width, height, font size, direction. Pure functions; heavy unit tests on synthetic items.
- Steps: normalise item boxes (handle rotation 0/90/180/270), merge items into words/lines by baseline and gap (gap threshold from font size; insert a space when the gap > ~0.25 em), detect columns (projection profile / whitespace gutter analysis over the page), order blocks (XY-cut is a good start), join lines into paragraphs (line spacing + indentation + ending punctuation), de-hyphenate line-end hyphens when the next line starts lowercase, detect headings by font size relative to the page body size (only when outline is absent).
- Right-to-left scripts: keep logical order from the content stream when items carry `dir: rtl`.
- Determinism: no floating-point order dependence — sort with stable keys and fixed rounding.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Synthetic tests: single column, two columns, three columns, column + full-width title, footnotes at page bottom, hyphenation, superscripts, rotated page.
- [ ] Golden tests on corpus PDFs, with a short human review note per file in the PR.
- [ ] Reading-order accuracy measured on 10 hand-checked pages and recorded in the PR (start of QA-7).
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes and CI is green

## Tests required

- [ ] Unit tests
- [ ] Golden tests (corpus files + reviewed expected output)

## Out of scope

- Table detection (PDF-8, P2).

## Blocked by

- #45 pdf: text layer per page, page labels, needsOcr, metadata, outline, links (PDF-1, 4, 6, 10)

issues.body:

Encrypted PDFs open with an empty user password when allowed, accept a `password` option, and otherwise throw `EncryptedError`.

**Requirements:** PDF-5 — see [docs/prd.md](https://github.com/sanjay3290/docsluice/blob/main/docs/prd.md).

issues.title: archives: GZIP and TAR
issues.body:
## Goal

`.gz` files give one child (the decompressed file); `.tar` (and `.tar.gz`) give one child per entry, under the shared budget.

**Requirements:** section 8.1 (Archives), SEC-1, NST-1..NST-6 — see [docs/prd.md](https://github.com/sanjay3290/docsluice/blob/main/docs/prd.md).

## Context and pointers

- gzip: header (FNAME, FEXTRA, FCOMMENT, FHCRC), multi-member, inflate through the same counted fflate path as zip. Ratio limit applies.
- tar: ustar, pax extended headers (path, size), GNU long names; checksum check; skip non-regular entries (symlinks listed, never followed).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Golden tests: .gz of a CSV, .tar with nested folders, .tar.gz.
- [ ] Hostile: gzip bomb, tar size lies, pax header bombs.
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes and CI is green

## Tests required

- [ ] Golden tests (corpus files + reviewed expected output)
- [ ] Hostile files added to `hostile/manifest.json`

issues.title: plugin: OCR interface and @docsluice/ocr-tesseract (EXT-5)
issues.body:
## Goal

A documented OCR interface in the core and a first-party tesseract.js adapter package that fills text for pages and images that need OCR.

**Requirements:** EXT-5, PDF-4, section 3 (OCR not in core), [ADR 0004](https://github.com/sanjay3290/docsluice/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-packaging.md) — see [docs/prd.md](https://github.com/sanjay3290/docsluice/blob/main/docs/prd.md).

## Context and pointers

- Core: `ocr?: OcrProvider` option where `OcrProvider = (image: { bytes: Uint8Array; mimeType: string }, opts: { language?: string; signal?: AbortSignal }) => Promise<{ text: string; confidence: number; boxes?: … }>`. The core never bundles OCR.
- Where it runs: PDF pages with `needsOcr` (the core does not render pages: use the largest page image XObject when it covers the page; document that vector-only pages need a renderer plugin), image files, and image children when asked. OCR text becomes paragraphs with `loc` and a confidence noted in warnings when low.
- Package `packages/ocr-tesseract` (`@docsluice/ocr-tesseract`): wraps tesseract.js, local only, language data path configurable, worker reuse. Its own README and tests (marked slow).
- A "bring your own function" example for a cloud vision API in the docs (no SDK dependency).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Scanned corpus PDF gives text through the plugin in Node.
- [ ] Core bundle size unchanged by the OCR interface (size check).
- [ ] Docs page with both adapters.
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes and CI is green

## Tests required

- [ ] Unit tests
- [ ] Golden tests (corpus files + reviewed expected output)

## Out of scope

- Page rendering of vector PDFs (P2 plugin).

## Blocked by

- #45 pdf: text layer per page, page labels, needsOcr, metadata, outline, links (PDF-1, 4, 6, 10)
- #41 plugin API: registerFormat() with contract version (EXT-4, EXT-7)
- #74 core: inline runs, child bytes, table-split chunks, exported building blocks (MOD-3, NST-5, CHK-4, EXT-6)

Follow the loop in [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/sanjay3290/docsluice/blob/main/AGENTS.md): read, check blockers, branch, draft PR, test first, verify, finish. Hard rules and the Definition of Done are in the same file. In Claude Code: `/work-issue <this number>`.
